cause: The private detached ref context solved symbolic-HEAD races by separating branch publication from the real worktree HEAD, but the design inventory covered content, refs, locks, hooks, and return state without treating the worktree-local reflog as a required publication side effect.
prevention: Specify recovery and audit artifacts as first-class transaction outputs; require normal and linked-worktree HEAD and branch reflog parity tests, exact symbolic-ref authorization, compare-and-swap publication, and fail-closed capability detection instead of manual or symlinked reflog fabrication.
summary: The sealed claim commit updated the authorized branch and its reflog but omitted the actual normal or linked worktree HEAD reflog expected for recovery and audit.
title: Protected publication must preserve the worktree recovery trail
